briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East conflict has sharply escalated over the past 24 hours, characterized by extensive US air strikes against Iranian military and civilian targets, met by widespread Iranian retaliatory missile and drone attacks on US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. Concurrently, the US re-imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports, prompting Iran to threaten closure of the Strait of Hormuz, thus significantly amplifying regional instability and the risk of a broader confrontation.

IRAN
US military operations against Iran continued with multiple waves of airstrikes, including a continuous seven-hour assault, targeting missile and drone sites, naval capabilities, and coastal defense systems. Reported civilian infrastructure damage includes two wheat storage facilities in Hoveyzeh and Dasht-e Azadegan, and a mineral water production facility in Ilam province. Military targets struck include army barracks in Bampur/Iranshahr (Tier 388), the Chahbahar port control tower (hit twice), and a naval base in Sirik. Explosions were reported in Shiraz (later clarified by Iran as routine industrial activity), Ahvaz, Qeshm, Kish, Mahshahr, Abadan, Andimeshk, Bushehr, and Khorramshahr.

The Iranian Army reported 7 military personnel martyred in US attacks in Iranshahr, while the Iranian government spokesperson claimed over 30 civilians were killed in recent US attacks. The Ministry of Health reported over 260 injured, including 3 women and 6 under 18, with 2 women among the martyred. Some sources, including Kian Meli 1 and Omid Dana, claimed significantly higher military casualties, potentially dozens to hundreds, in the Bampur/Iranshahr barracks strike.

Iran launched several waves of retaliatory missile and drone strikes (Operations Nasr 2 and Sa'eqah/Thunder) targeting US military facilities in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan. Specific targets included the satellite communications center, missile and air defense radar, Patriot air defense complex, logistics facilities, and HIMARS missile launch platforms at US military bases in Kuwait. In Bahrain, Iran targeted the NSI management center, command and control center, large warehouses of military parts and equipment, and fuel depots of the US Fifth Fleet. In Jordan, strikes hit the Al-Azraq airbase, specifically targeting F-15, F-16, and F-35 fighter jet quarters and strategic US drones. The IRGC issued messages to the people of Kuwait and Jordan, urging them to expel US forces, asserting that the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until US aggression ends. Iran rejected President Trump’s claim of 11-hour talks in Oman, stating no direct negotiations were held. Internally, Mohammad Amini Dehkhani was executed for arson during January 2026 protests. The Central Bank of Iran's digital wallets were sanctioned by the US Treasury, freezing over $130 million.

ISRAEL
Israeli military forces conducted an aerial strike in northern Gaza, killing two Hamas Nukhba Force commanders, Ali Shamlakh and Nasser Louh, identified as advancing attacks and training operatives. In a separate operation in Jabalia, Mohammed Marwan Mohammed Salem, chief of security for Hamas’s Central Jabalia Battalion, was killed along with several other Hamas operatives, including Abd al-Malek Abu al-Jabin (Nukhba Force and Hamas police chief of investigations), Yaman Mohammed Jibril Ubaid (Central Jabalia Battalion), and Ghassan Akram Salama Dakas (West Jabalia Battalion and Hamas police). These operatives were reportedly gathered to advance terror plots.

An Israeli soldier in mandatory service was sentenced to 5 years in prison for espionage, having sent two videos of missile interceptions and a missile impact from civilian locations to an Iranian handler during the June 2025 "Roar of the Lion" war with Iran. Michael Katz, an 82-year-old senior engineer at Rafael Advanced Defense Systems, died from injuries sustained from an Iranian missile attack in Haifa in April, becoming a confirmed casualty of the conflict.

Politically, the Knesset approved a controversial law (58-54 votes) to freeze the arrests of Yeshiva students who are draft dodgers. This decision was met with protests by ultra-Orthodox groups outside recruitment centers in Tel HaShomer and Jerusalem and drew strong criticism from opposition figures, with petitions immediately filed to the High Court against the law. MK Sharen Haskel resigned as Deputy Foreign Minister, accusing Minister Gidon Sa'ar of lying. Prime Minister Netanyahu visited the Dimona nuclear reactor and warned Iran that any new attack would be met with a "much more powerful" response. Netanyahu is expected to travel to Washington, D.C. on Saturday evening, with a potential meeting with President Trump and attendance at Senator Lindsey Graham's funeral on Tuesday. Separately, Duvdevan unit fighters arrested two individuals suspected of manufacturing explosives targeting IDF forces in the Binyamin sector.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces conducted aerial strikes in northern Gaza, resulting in the elimination of two Hamas Nukhba Force commanders, Ali Shamlakh and Nasser Louh, deemed an immediate threat to Israeli troops. Further strikes in the Jabalia area killed Mohammed Marwan Mohammed Salem, the security chief of Hamas's Central Jabalia Battalion, and several other operatives including Abd al-Malek Abu al-Jabin, Yaman Mohammed Jibril Ubaid, and Ghassan Akram Salama Dakas, who were reportedly gathering to advance terror plots.

In the West Bank, two wanted individuals involved in manufacturing explosives to target IDF forces were arrested by Duvdevan unit fighters in the Binyamin sector. An Israeli civilian was lightly injured by stone-throwing at her vehicle on Road 60 near Ma'ale Levona, leading to a cordon placed on the village of Sinjil and searches for suspects. Reconstruction efforts in Gaza are reportedly stalled due to security threats. A group of Israeli settler activists from the "Uri Tzafon Movement," including one adult and four minors, briefly crossed into Lebanon near Ghajar before being returned by the IDF and handed over to police for questioning.

LEBANON
Israeli forces conducted an artillery strike targeting the town of Qunin and Wadi Al-Hajir in southern Lebanon. A drone strike was also reported in the village of Nabatieh al-Fouqa in southern Lebanon. A group of Israeli settler activists, comprising one adult and four minors from the Uri Tzafon Movement, reportedly crossed the border into Lebanon near the community of Ghajar by "several meters" before being located and returned to Israeli territory by the IDF. They were subsequently handed over to the police for questioning, with their movement advocating for settlement in southern Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Iraq's Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi announced alongside US President Trump that all US military forces would depart Iraq by September 30. Iran-backed Kata'ib Hezbollah in Iraq declared that their participation and that of other resistance forces would be "immediate and decisive" if war erupts in Iran. Separately, Iraqi authorities placed Lebanon's Hezbollah on a banking sanctions list, citing US Executive Order 13224 related to combating terrorism financing networks, which Iraqi sources attributed to US wishes. A drone reportedly crashed in an Iraqi port, with port authorities stating it did not affect operational activities. Reports indicate Iranian drones entered Syrian airspace over Deir ez-Zor.

GULF STATES
The Gulf region is experiencing heightened tensions with direct Iranian retaliatory strikes against US military facilities. Kuwait's military reported intercepting one ballistic missile, five cruise missiles, and 33 drones, noting damage to a Kuwaiti Navy vessel and injuries to four personnel. Iran stated that its "Operation Nasr 2" successfully targeted satellite communications centers, missile and air defense radars, Patriot air defense complexes, logistics facilities, and HIMARS missile launch platforms at US military bases in Kuwait.

In Bahrain, the IRGC's "Operation Nasr 2" targeted the US Fifth Fleet's NSI management center, command and control center, large military equipment warehouses, and fuel depots, with satellite imagery reportedly showing damage to a drone command center at the US Fifth Fleet base in Juffair. Bahrain's Ministry of Interior issued urgent alerts, sounding sirens and advising citizens to seek safe locations. Satellite images also suggested emergency gas flaring at an LPG refinery in Saudi Arabia, near Jubail Industrial City, following an incident.

US President Trump announced he would not impose a 20% toll on Strait of Hormuz transits, instead opting for "trade and investment deals" with Gulf states, which he claimed would be "historic." However, the European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) issued a warning to airlines against flying over Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE, and the Persian Gulf due to heightened risks. Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry strongly condemned Iran's attacks on multiple Arab nations, including Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Jordan, and Emirati oil tankers, holding Tehran responsible for the consequences and calling for an end to the destabilizing actions. Two Iranian oil tankers were rerouted to Karachi, Pakistan.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Intensified US Strikes on Iran:** US forces launched multiple waves of airstrikes against military and civilian targets across Iran, including a sustained seven-hour operation, hitting missile/drone sites, naval capabilities, and infrastructure like wheat storage facilities.
2.  **Widespread Iranian Retaliatory Strikes:** Iran executed several waves of missile and drone attacks, targeting US military assets and bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, and Jordan (specifically Al-Azraq base), claiming to have destroyed command centers, air defense systems, and logistical facilities.
3.  **US Reinstates Naval Blockade on Iran:** CENTCOM announced the resumption of a full naval blockade on Iranian ports and vessels, effective July 14, 2026, 16:00 ET, citing Iranian attacks on commercial shipping.
4.  **Iran Threatens Strait of Hormuz Closure:** The IRGC declared the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed as long as US aggression continues, asserting "oil and gas exports are either available to all or available to none."
5.  **Significant Casualties in Iran:** Iran’s Army reported 7 military personnel martyred in a US strike on the Iranshahr barracks, while the government spokesperson stated over 30 civilians were killed in recent US attacks.
6.  **Israeli Conscription Law Passed Amid Protests:** The Knesset approved a law freezing the arrest of Yeshiva students for draft evasion (58-54 votes), sparking ultra-Orthodox protests at recruitment centers and immediate High Court petitions.
7.  **Hamas Commanders Eliminated in Gaza:** Israeli forces killed at least two Nukhba Force commanders (Ali Shamlakh, Nasser Louh) and the security chief of the Central Jabalia Battalion (Mohammed Marwan Mohammed Salem) along with other operatives in targeted strikes in northern Gaza and Jabalia.
8.  **Israeli Soldier Sentenced for Espionage:** A serving Israeli soldier received a five-year prison sentence for contact with an Iranian agent and delivering information (videos of missile interceptions and impacts) during the June 2025 war with Iran.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of widespread regional conflict has significantly escalated, with active flashpoints across Iran, the Persian Gulf, and US bases in allied Gulf states and Jordan. The direct and sustained military exchanges between the US and Iran, coupled with Iran's explicit retaliatory actions against multiple US military installations, signal a shift towards a more direct and confrontational phase of hostilities. The reinstatement of a US naval blockade on Iranian ports, met by Iran's threat to close the Strait of Hormuz, establishes a critical red line with severe global economic implications and a high potential for direct naval confrontation.

President Trump's threats of wider attacks on Iranian energy infrastructure and bridges, juxtaposed with his call for negotiations, indicate a coercive strategy aimed at forcing Iranian concessions, but also present a clear escalation pathway. Iran's reports of significant military and civilian casualties and its defiant rhetoric underscore a commitment to continued retaliation. The declared US military exit from Iraq by September 30 introduces a power vacuum risk, potentially emboldening Iran-backed militias like Kata'ib Hezbollah, which has pledged immediate participation in any war against Iran. The presence of Israeli settler activists in southern Lebanon further complicates the already tense Israeli-Lebanese border, risking unintended cross-border incidents.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **United States** has significantly escalated its posture, launching new waves of airstrikes across Iran and implementing a full naval blockade on Iranian ports. President Trump threatened "much harder" strikes targeting Iran's power plants and bridges next week if Iran does not come to the negotiating table, while simultaneously backing down on a 20% Strait of Hormuz toll in favor of Gulf state investments. The US Senate Democrats, however, blocked a $1.15 trillion defense bill over objections to the Iran war.

**Gulf States** are caught in the escalating conflict, with Kuwait and Bahrain directly targeted by Iranian retaliatory strikes against US bases on their soil, confirming interceptions and injuries. Saudi Arabia, along with other Gulf states, condemned Iran's attacks, holding Tehran responsible for regional instability. The **European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA)** issued a warning to airlines against flying over Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, UAE, and the Persian Gulf due to heightened risks, reflecting international concern over the safety of commercial aviation in the region.

**Russia's** spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, described the situation in the Persian Gulf as "critical," suggesting the US has no immediate opportunity to resolve the Ukraine issue. Russia's military has continued operations in Ukraine, intercepting 93 Ukrainian drones, while Ukraine claimed to have attacked 20 Russian ships, including 17 oil tankers, in the Black Sea. **China's** economy grew at its slowest pace in three years, and reports suggest growing cracks in its alliance with Russia, including Chinese espionage on Russian officials. **Turkey's** President Erdogan was mentioned by Netanyahu, who stated that Erdogan should not receive weapons, as he "makes them himself," indicating a degree of Israeli skepticism towards Turkey.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are significant discrepancies in casualty reporting from the US strikes on Iran. While the Iranian Army announced 7 military personnel martyred in Iranshahr, the government spokesperson claimed over 30 civilian deaths, and local sources (Kian Meli 1, Omid Dana) reported potentially dozens to hundreds of military casualties in the same incident, with Omid Dana accusing the regime of using soldiers as human shields. These divergent figures suggest potential underreporting by official Iranian military sources or exaggerated claims by opposition/local channels for propaganda purposes.

The claim by PressTV that the US killed "Imam Khamenei" and 168 children at "Minab School" "more than four months ago" as the start of the war is highly contradictory and appears to be a propaganda fabrication. Official PressTV reports also mention a "historic funeral" for Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, implying his recent death (July 14, 2026), which directly conflicts with the "four months ago" timeline and the notion of him being martyred as the *start* of the current conflict. This constitutes a significant propaganda indicator, potentially aimed at eliciting a specific emotional or political response by conflating events or misrepresenting facts. The "death to Trump" poster in Tehran's Revolution Square is a clear indicator of Iranian state-sponsored propaganda.

There are reporting gaps regarding the specifics of damage and long-term impact of both US and Iranian strikes, particularly in the Gulf states, with many reports of "explosions" without confirmed targets or precise damage assessments. The exact timing and locations of all claimed Iranian retaliatory strikes are not fully consistent across sources, indicating potential delays or incomplete information. The nature of "industrial activity" causing explosions in Shiraz is also an unverified claim from Iranian media.
